notation.ambient_space: A denotes the MeasurableSpace instance on Omega with respect to which the input Measure mu is given. F, or F_t, is a separately supplied measurable space on the same carrier.
notation.indices: Natural indices include zero. H_t={0,...,t-1} is the subtype corresponding to Finset.range t. The sum over Finset.range T has exactly T terms and is empty at T=0.
notation.real_measurable_space: Real-valued maps use the usual Borel measurable space. Finite history spaces use the coordinate product measurable space, and their product with Seed uses the product measurable space.
notation.measurable_space_order: F <= G means every F-measurable set is G-measurable. F contains at most the information in G, not the reverse.
notation.ae: For all-mu-almost-every omega means that the exceptional subset has mu-measure zero in the ambient measure's all-set/outer-measure sense. The exceptional subset itself need not be an A-measurable set in an incomplete space.
notation.independence: IndepFun U V mu asserts independence of the two random maps: for measurable target sets B,C, mu(U^{-1}(B) intersect V^{-1}(C)) equals mu(U^{-1}(B)) times mu(V^{-1}(C)). For real-valued targets these are Borel test sets. iIndepFun Y mu is mutual independence of the indexed family, involving every finite subfamily, not just pairwise independence.
notation.identical_distribution: IdentDistrib (Y t) (Y 0) mu mu asserts equality of their distributions under the indicated same measure (with the corresponding almost-everywhere measurability requirements in the standard notion). Here ordinary measurability of every Y t is additionally explicit.

privateSeedPastInformation.formula: Let H_t(omega)=(S(omega),(Y_i(omega))_{0<=i<t}). Then G_t=privateSeedPastInformation S Y t is the pullback sigma-algebra H_t^{-1}(B(Seed x R^{H_t})). A subset of Omega belongs to G_t exactly when it is the preimage under H_t of a measurable subset of that data space.
privateSeedPastInformation.meaning: It is precisely the sigma-algebra generated by the measurable observations of S and the finite strictly past real coordinates Y_0,...,Y_{t-1}. This definition makes sense even when S and Y are not measurable relative to the separately supplied ambient A.
privateSeedPastInformation.zero_time: H_0 has no real observation coordinate. Its history component is the unique function from the empty type. G_0 is therefore the sigma-algebra pulled back from S alone.
privateSeedPastInformation.limits: The definition by itself asserts neither independence nor secrecy of S, nor ordinary measurability of S or Y with respect to A. No current value Y_t or future value occurs.

expectedFixedMinimum.formula: For a single deterministic real u in [0,1], let L_T(u)=integral_Omega sum_{t=0}^{T-1}(u-Y_t(omega))^2 dmu. Then M_T=inf{L_T(u):u in [0,1]}.
expectedFixedMinimum.quantifier_and_optimization_order: The same scalar u is used at every time and every sample point. First integrate its cumulative loss, then take the infimum over u. This is not integral of a pointwise infimum, not the expected realized best-comparator loss, not an optimization over random u(omega), and not an optimization over a time-varying sequence.
expectedFixedMinimum.definition_level_limits: The definition supplies no probability, measurability, or integrability hypotheses. It uses Lean's real-valued Bochner integral, which is totalized and equals zero outside its integrable regime; it is not an extended-real expectation that returns positive infinity for every divergent nonnegative function. The sInf is an infimum in R. Each displayed squared-loss integral is nonnegative under these conventions, and the image is nonempty because [0,1] is nonempty, so this image is bounded below. Attainment is not part of the definition.
expectedFixedMinimum.empty_horizon: For T=0 every loss sum is zero, L_0(u)=0 for every u, and M_0=0.

expectedFixedRegret.meaning: It subtracts the infimum of expected fixed-scalar losses from expected prediction loss. The baseline is determined by mu, Y, and T, not by a separately supplied comparator or by each realized sample path.
expectedFixedRegret.definition_level_limits: No feasibility, causality, independence, or integrability assumption is bundled into this definition. The same totalized real-integral convention applies. Under T4's hypotheses the relevant integrals are finite genuine integrals of almost-everywhere measurable bounded losses.

eventuallyMeasurableSpace.exact_set_level_meaning: For a measurable space F on Omega, E_mu(F)=eventuallyMeasurableSpace F (ae mu) has measurable subsets A exactly when there exists B in F such that the indicator-membership predicates of A and B agree mu-almost everywhere. Equivalently, mu(A symmetric_difference B)=0. The provided definition uses one such witness B for each set A, with the exceptional set allowed to depend on A.
eventuallyMeasurableSpace.function_level_meaning: P is measurable from E_mu(F) to R exactly when for each Borel C subset R, P^{-1}(C) differs on a mu-null subset from some F-measurable subset of Omega. At this assumption stage those witnesses and null subsets may depend on C. T1 supplies the stronger function-level representation by one F-measurable real function equal to P outside one null set.
eventuallyMeasurableSpace.not_time_eventuality: The word eventually refers to the filter ae mu. It does not refer to large natural times, a limiting horizon, or an eventual tail of the process.
eventuallyMeasurableSpace.ambient_measure_caveat: The null ideal comes from the ambient measure mu, while F is supplied independently. T1 and T2 do not assume F <= A. One must not silently replace this construction by the ordinary completion of the restriction of mu to F. Even with F <= A, this construction allows all ambient mu-null modifications; a null set need not be covered by an F-measurable null set, as the usual completion of the restricted measure would require.
eventuallyMeasurableSpace.why_sigma_algebra: The supplied upstream definition has a CountableInterFilter hypothesis. The ae filter has the required countable stability, allowing countably many exceptional null sets to be combined. No finiteness or probability assumption on mu is required for this construction.

targets.natural_mathematical_statement: For every measurable carrier (Omega,A), every measure mu on A, every sigma-algebra F on Omega, and every real-valued P measurable with respect to E_mu(F), there exists a real-valued version V which is F-measurable and satisfies P=V mu-almost everywhere.

seven_slots.1_objects_spaces: Omega is arbitrary, mu is an arbitrary measure, F is an arbitrary second sigma-algebra on the same carrier, and P,V map Omega to Borel R. No standard-Borel or probability-space hypothesis is imposed on Omega.
seven_slots.2_quantifiers_order: For all Omega,A,mu,F,P satisfying the sole measurability hypothesis, there exists V. V may depend on all these inputs. Both F-measurability of V and almost-everywhere equality hold for that same V.
seven_slots.3_assumptions: P is measurable from E_mu(F) to Borel R. No mu(Omega)=1, finite measure, sigma-finite measure, F<=A, boundedness, integrability, or ordinary A-measurability of P is assumed.
seven_slots.4_conclusion_metric: Existence of an F-measurable version, with exact equality almost everywhere. This is not an approximation in norm, an equality at every point, or a uniqueness claim for V.
seven_slots.5_constants_normalization: No numerical constants, normalization, rates, or horizon appear.
seven_slots.6_probability_information_null_sets: There is one exceptional null subset outside which equality of the full real values holds. That subset may depend on P,F,mu and V. No stochastic independence or filtration is asserted. If F is not a sub-sigma-algebra of A, the conclusion does not itself assert that V is A-measurable.
seven_slots.7_boundaries_exclusions: The theorem applies to arbitrary measures, including the zero measure and infinite measures. Under the zero measure the equality requirement is vacuous, while V must still be F-measurable. Its target is R; no assertion for arbitrary non-countably-generated target measurable spaces is written.

targets.natural_mathematical_statement: Let Omega and Seed be arbitrary measurable spaces, mu any measure on Omega, Y_n any real functions on Omega, and S any Seed-valued function. Let F_n be any family of sigma-algebras satisfying F_t<=G_t, where G_t is the information generated by S and Y_0,...,Y_{t-1}. Suppose every prediction_t is E_mu(F_t)-measurable and lies in [0,1] mu-almost everywhere. Then there exists a family of measurable functions p_t:Seed x R^{H_t}->R, each taking values in [0,1] at every input, such that outside one mu-null subset, simultaneously for every natural t, prediction_t(omega)=p_t(S(omega),(Y_i(omega))_{i<t}).

seven_slots.1_objects_spaces: Arbitrary measurable Omega and Seed; arbitrary measure mu; arbitrary Y:N->Omega->R and S:Omega->Seed; a family F:N->MeasurableSpace(Omega); and real predictions. Each policy domain is the measurable product of Seed and the t-coordinate finite real history space. There is no topological or standard-Borel assumption on Seed.
seven_slots.2_quantifiers_order: Universally quantify the spaces, mu,Y,S,F with all-time inclusion, and prediction with its two all-time hypotheses. Then existentially choose one family policy indexed by every natural t. For this same family: every policy_t is measurable; for every t and every input q its value belongs to [0,1]; and for almost every omega, for every t the representation equality holds. The last order is AE omega then ALL t, not merely ALL t then AE omega.
seven_slots.3_assumptions: For every t, F_t<=G_t; prediction_t is measurable from E_mu(F_t) to R; and prediction_t is in [0,1] almost everywhere. Mu need not be a probability measure. Ordinary ambient measurability of Y or S is not assumed. There is no independence hypothesis. F is not required to be increasing, so the name family of information spaces must not be inflated to a filtration assumption.
seven_slots.4_conclusion_metric: An exact almost-everywhere functional representation on the observed seed and strict finite history, with policies measurable and feasible everywhere. The policies are defined on all possible inputs, including inputs not attained by any omega. No uniqueness, continuity, computability, or preservation of values on exceptional sample points is asserted.
seven_slots.5_constants_normalization: Feasibility is the closed interval [0,1], including both endpoints. No error tolerance, rate, or finite horizon parameter appears.
seven_slots.6_probability_information_null_sets: Each input feasibility hypothesis permits its own null exception at each t. The conclusion asserts a single null exceptional subset valid for all countably many t. That common subset can depend on the supplied entire process and the chosen policy family. No common null set uniform across all possible input processes is claimed. The policy receives S and Y_i for i<t, never Y_t or a future coordinate. S is merely an input here; independence, privateness, or stochastic generation of it is not asserted. Equality is modulo the ambient mu-null ideal even if F_t or G_t is not contained in the ambient A.
seven_slots.7_boundaries_exclusions: Every natural t is covered, including t=0. At t=0 the history argument has a single possible value and policy_0 may depend only on S. There is no separate prescribed initialization. Boundedness holds for every policy input at every time, while equality with the original predictions holds only almost everywhere. Timewise measurability is explicit; no separate joint-measurability assertion on an encoded varying-domain total space is stated.

targets.natural_mathematical_statement: On any probability space (Omega,A,mu), let the real maps Y_n be measurable and mutually independent. Let S:Omega->Seed be measurable and independent of the entire trajectory map omega -> (Y_n(omega))_{n in N}. Fix any natural t and any sigma-algebra F contained in G_t, the information generated by S and the strict past Y_0,...,Y_{t-1}. Every real map P measurable with respect to E_mu(F) is independent of Y_t under mu.

seven_slots.1_objects_spaces: Arbitrary measurable Omega and Seed, probability measure mu, a countable family of real random variables, a measurable Seed-valued S, one fixed natural t, one sigma-algebra F, and one real-valued P. The full trajectory takes values in the countable product R^N with its product sigma-algebra.
seven_slots.2_quantifiers_order: Universally choose mu,Y with hY and mutual independence, then S with measurability and trajectory independence, then t,F with inclusion, then P with E_mu(F)-measurability. The conclusion holds for every such choice. No existence of P or F is being asserted and no choice of P is fixed across all t by this declaration.
seven_slots.3_assumptions: Mu is a probability measure. Each Y_n is ordinarily A-measurable. The whole family Y is mutually independent. S is ordinarily measurable and independent of the full trajectory, which is stronger than the statement that S is separately independent of each individual coordinate. F<=G_t. P is E_mu(F)-measurable. No identical-distribution, boundedness, integrability, zero-mean, or finite-variance assumption on Y or P is present.
seven_slots.4_conclusion_metric: IndepFun P (Y_t) mu: independence of this prediction-like real map and the current real observation. For Borel B,C this is the product formula for the two preimage events. It is not conditional independence given S, a moment factorization without integrability conditions, or an assertion that P is independent of the full trajectory.
seven_slots.5_constants_normalization: The only normalization is mu(Omega)=1. There are no numeric loss bounds or rates and no positive-time restriction.
seven_slots.6_probability_information_null_sets: P may differ on an ambient null subset from an F-measurable representative. The conclusion is a law-level independence assertion for P itself, stable under such null changes. Ordinary A-measurability of the literal P is not explicitly required or concluded; almost-everywhere measurable representatives suffice for the stated semantics. Since hY and hS hold here, G_t is contained in A, hence so is F. F need not contain the full past information, only be a sub-sigma-algebra of it. There is no indexed filtration assumption.
seven_slots.7_boundaries_exclusions: At t=0 the past is empty and G_0 is generated by S alone, so the conclusion includes seed-only choices modulo null sets. The theorem covers any fixed finite natural t. No stopping time, random index, infinitely long history, adaptive observation selection, or randomized algorithm class beyond the explicit seed model is quantified over.

targets.natural_mathematical_statement: On a probability space, let Y_n be measurable, mutually independent, identically distributed with Y_0, and in [0,1] almost everywhere for every n. Let S be measurable and independent of the entire Y trajectory. Let F_t<=G_t for every natural t. Let prediction_t be E_mu(F_t)-measurable and in [0,1] almost everywhere for every t. Write m=integral Y_0 dmu. For every natural horizon T, the expected prediction loss minus the infimum, over a fixed deterministic u in [0,1], of its expected cumulative squared loss equals sum_{t=0}^{T-1} integral (prediction_t-m)^2 dmu, and this regret is nonnegative.

seven_slots.1_objects_spaces: Arbitrary measurable Omega and Seed, probability measure mu, a countable real observation process, one Seed-valued random map, a time-indexed family of sigma-algebras, a real prediction process, and a finite natural horizon T. Squared losses and all integrals in the conclusion are real-valued.
seven_slots.2_quantifiers_order: Universally quantify mu,Y and hY,hlaw,hb,hind, then S,hS,hseed, then F and all-time hF, then prediction and all-time hP,hpb, and finally an arbitrary T:N. For the same inputs and horizon the conclusion is a conjunction: exact equality AND nonnegativity. All process assumptions apply to every natural time, even though a particular conclusion uses only indices below T.
seven_slots.3_assumptions: Mu(Omega)=1. Every Y_t is A-measurable. For every t, Y_t and Y_0 have the same distribution under mu. For every t, Y_t belongs to [0,1] mu-almost everywhere. Y is mutually independent. S is measurable and independent of the entire real trajectory. For every t, F_t<=G_t; prediction_t is E_mu(F_t)-measurable; and prediction_t belongs to [0,1] mu-almost everywhere. No monotonicity of F is assumed. No ordinary A-measurability of the literal predictions is explicitly required.
seven_slots.4_conclusion_metric: Let m=integral_Omega Y_0(omega)dmu. Then R_T=sum_{t<T} integral_Omega (prediction_t(omega)-m)^2 dmu and 0<=R_T. This is an exact expected-loss decomposition with a deterministic fixed-comparator benchmark. It is not a realized sample-path identity, not expected regret to a best hindsight comparator chosen separately on each sample path, and not a statement that every realized loss difference is nonnegative.
seven_slots.5_constants_normalization: The observation and prediction interval is exactly [0,1]. The coefficient of each squared-error term is 1. The benchmark center is the unconditional mean m of Y_0, not a sample mean, conditional mean, or time-dependent empirical estimate. There is no factor 1/T, no additive remainder, and no rate or asymptotic notation. All expectations are with respect to the same probability measure mu.
seven_slots.6_probability_information_null_sets: The hypotheses hb and hpb each have the order ALL t then AE omega. Their exceptional subsets may initially depend on t; countability allows a common full-measure set, but no pointwise bounds on all omega are assumed. The measurability hypothesis permits ambient-null modifications of F_t-measurable functions. With hY and hS, F_t<=G_t<=A, so those modifications yield ambient almost-everywhere measurability and, with boundedness, integrability of the finite losses. Mu includes both seed and outcome randomness. Seed independence concerns the full trajectory, and strict past information plus mutual independence prevents prediction_t from having distributional information about the current independent Y_t. The conclusion is an equality of real integrals, not an event whose probability is being lower-bounded. It introduces no additional exceptional subset and no confidence parameter.
seven_slots.7_boundaries_exclusions: Every finite natural horizon T is allowed, including T=0. At zero both cumulative losses, the fixed-comparator infimum, R_0, and the right-hand sum are zero, so the conclusion is 0=0 and 0<=0. T=1 includes the time-zero prediction, whose allowable information is the seed plus null modifications and whose bound is almost everywhere. T includes precisely indices 0 through T-1; Y_T is absent. No infinite horizon, random stopping horizon, conditional expectation claim, high-probability bound, adversarial-outcome guarantee, or convergence/sublinear-rate conclusion is written.

interpretive_consequences_not_additional: The assumptions imply m in [0,1]. The deterministic comparator m is admissible.

Expanding the identical-distribution squared losses gives L_T(u)=T*((u-m)^2+integral (Y_0-m)^2 dmu), and hence M_T=T*integral (Y_0-m)^2 dmu. This explains the benchmark in the equality; it is a derivation from the hypotheses, not a separately displayed clause of T4.
For T>0 the expected fixed loss is uniquely minimized by u=m. For T=0 every u in [0,1] minimizes it. No uniqueness of a policy is implied.

The assertion of nonnegative expected regret does not assert it is strictly positive. For example, predictions equal to m almost everywhere at all contributing times make the displayed right-hand side zero.
